Jonas,

Thanks for the call today — appreciate the walkthrough of Redwood Dedicated and the autoscaling options. We want to run a short simulation before committing to reserved capacity so procurement can see cost/SLA tradeoffs under our peak marketing events (Black Friday-ish traffic).

A few ask items we promised on the call: 
- We can share a 2-week traffic export (anonymized). Is CSV OK?
- Need a simple matrix from Redwood: concurrency -> GPU count -> estimated p95/p99 latency for text-generation (for our prompt mix).
- Can Redwood show a burst-mode example where QPS spikes 10x for 3 minutes, then drops? We want to see queuing behavior + cold-start effects.

I attached a small sample export and our high-level prompt mix.

Best,
Caroline
Head of Platform Engineering
FastRetail

Subject: Re: sizing for dedicated fleet — next steps

Caroline — thanks for sending the sample. Looping in Marissa for the technical sizing and Vivek for capacity economics. Ben, bringing you in for procurement cadence.

Short answers up-front: CSV is perfect. We typically ask for: token-level histograms (prompt tokens, completion tokens), per-request QPS timestamps (UTC), and a list of critical endpoints that need p95/p99 SLOs. With that we can run a 48‑hour simulation and a focused burst scenario.

To get us started, please confirm these three additional details in the attached checklist: 
1) Typical completion lengths per endpoint (median / 95th).
2) Desired latency SLOs (p95 and p99) per endpoint.
3) Whether you can tolerate queueing during sustained spikes, or you require elastic autoscaling with guaranteed warm capacity.

I'll run an initial back-of-envelope while the team analyzes the CSV. Expect a simulation workbook back by EOD Wednesday.

— Jonas Weber
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: burst-sla-simulation-template.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Caroline Myers <caroline.myers@fastretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sizing for dedicated fleet — next steps

Caroline, team — quick technical notes from the workload intake pass. I imported the CSV and pulled a few high-level numbers: 
- Baseline QPS (weekday daytime): 180 qps across 12 endpoints.
- Peak short bursts observed: single-minute spikes up to 2,000 qps (we assume clients will throttle to 1,200 qps on the API layer).
- Prompt tokens: median 36, completion median 128; 95th completion token = 640 tokens.
- Token distribution skewed: ~20% of requests are long completions (>=512 tokens) and drive GPU memory pressure.

Recommendations / open tradeoffs: 
- Warm capacity: for 1,200 qps sustained bursts with 95th completions at 640 tokens, we recommend baseline reserved fleet of 8 A100-class GPUs (or 12x A10 equivalent) plus 2 hot-standby nodes for fast failover.
- Autoscaling window: aggressive 30s scale-up with pre-warm buffer works for marketing bursts; otherwise queueing rises quickly.
- KV cache: enabling prefix cache for repeated user prompts reduces token compute by ~18% in our estimates — worth enabling for endpoints with repeat prompts.

Marissa — can you produce the concurrency->GPU mapping table (p95/p99 latency) by EOD? I'll annotate cost impact per mapping for Procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Ben Carter

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Caroline Myers <caroline.myers@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sizing for dedicated fleet — next steps

Caroline — quick note on economics and SLA backstops: 
- Using Marissa's perf curves, baseline of 8 A100s yields estimated p95 = 110ms, p99 = 420ms for median completions (128 tokens). Under the 10x single-minute burst (2,000 qps), with the optional hourly metered burst pool (4 additional nodes) we estimate p95 = 220ms, p99 = 1.6s and transient queuing for 20–45s while autoscaler brings more capacity online.
- If FastRetail requires hard p99 <= 500ms during bursts, we'd need a larger warm pool (approx 14 A100s warm) or a hybrid approach: 8 reserved + 6 pre-warm standby charged as reserved with lower nominal utilization.
- I'll attach a short table correlating concurrency buckets to GPU counts + monthly cost delta.

Next steps: Jonas will run the burst simulation workbook against the CSV and we’ll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough Wednesday morning PST. Caroline — does 10:00am PST on Wednesday work?

— Vivek
Director, Capacity Economics, Redwood Inference
